x: Rakhigarhi, the largest known Harappan settlement, lies in Hisar district, Haryana, on the seasonal Drishadvati. The other pairs are wrong: Lothal lies on the Bhogava (a Sabarmati tributary), not the Ghaggar; Rangpur on the Bhadar, not the Indus; and Dholavira on Khadir island in the Rann of Kutch, not on the Ravi.

The range 2450–1700 BCE belongs to Kayatha, not Jorwe, so D is the wrong pair. Ahar (2800–1500 BCE) and Malwa (1900–1400 BCE) are correctly dated; Jorwe is a later Chalcolithic culture (c. 1400–700 BCE).

The name Bharatavarsha is traced to the Bharata tribe. The Panchajana were only the Yadus, Turvasas, Anus, Druhyus and Purus; the Kikatas (south Bihar/Magadha) and Srinjayas were outside it, and the name is not derived from the Druhyus.

Charms and amulets point to a belief in ghosts and evil forces, against which they were presumably worn for protection. Amulets also show deities or persons in yogic poses; nothing links them to divine kingship or a ban on figurines.
The clay mask of a horned god is from Gujarat and Kalibangan, and the lifelike bearded terracotta males are grouped with it. The other site pairs are not linked to these figurines.
